subject: Pay-As-You-Throw and Bi-Weekly Trash Proposal
overview: The committee reviewed progress on the city's Climate Action Plan and received updates on municipal sustainability initiatives, including school air quality sensors and energy aggregation. A significant portion of the meeting was dedicated to debating a proposed pay-as-you-throw trash system and the transition to bi-weekly waste collection.

items.title: Minutes and Summer Schedule
items.summary: The committee approved the minutes from the previous meeting and discussed moving upcoming summer sessions to public outdoor spaces.

items.title: City Sustainability Updates
items.summary: Brenda Pike announced upcoming community events including a bicycling fair and reported that outdoor air quality sensors are now live at five local schools. The city signed a three-year strategic energy management plan with National Grid to secure additional efficiency incentives.

items.title: Electricity Aggregation and Third-Party Suppliers
items.summary: The committee reviewed a report from the Attorney General regarding resident losses to third-party electricity suppliers and discussed a webinar to educate the public. The city is updating its aggregation plan to automatically enroll low-income residents in the lowest available basic rate.

items.title: New High School Sustainability Goals
items.summary: Pike reported that the school committee voted to pursue LEED Platinum certification for the new high school project, which includes goals for full electrification and geothermal heating. The project aims for a 20% reduction in embodied carbon and net-zero energy operations.

items.title: Climate Action Plan Progress Review
items.summary: The committee walked through a progress tracking spreadsheet for the Climate Action Plan, covering items such as greenhouse gas modeling and zoning recodification. Members discussed new accessory dwelling unit laws and the establishment of the Municipal Affordable Housing Trust.

items.title: Legislative and Environmental Updates
items.summary: Lauretta James summarized pending state environmental legislation, including the Mass Ready Act, the Plastics Reduction Act, and a bill to restrict anticoagulant rodenticides. The committee discussed the impact of these toxins on local wildlife and potential municipal levers for enacting bans.

items.title: Pay-As-You-Throw and Waste Management Discussion
items.summary: The committee debated the merits and implementation challenges of a proposed pay-as-you-throw trash system and bi-weekly collection schedule. Discussion focused on rodent control, pet waste management, and the potential for municipal composting to reduce the volume of household trash.
